findings.text: blocking: `released()` reads `record["project"]` on the record `RunStore.retire` builds at reckon/run_store.py:1547 from `_decoded_record(payload)`, and reckon/run_store.py:966 `_split_durable` no longer writes `project` into that payload, so the retention sweep raises KeyError once any row written after this change is older than the cutoff; reproduced at head with a probe that appends one row through RunStore.append and calls retire(can_retire=lambda record: record["project"]), which prints "RESULT: KeyError: 'project'".

non-blocking: the sqlite fallback decodes a stored payload and asserts `row["project"] == project`, which the same payload change leaves unset, so the velocity reading raises AssertionError on any post-change row it reaches; the fallback fires only for promotions absent from the committed documents and the store, which makes it rarer than the gc path but the same defect.

non-blocking: the column-backfill migration calls `_query_values(..., record ...)` without `project=`, so it still derives the project from a payload that rows written after this change no longer carry; a future column addition re-runs this branch over those rows and would leave their project column NULL, hiding them from every project-filtered read.

non-blocking: `_run_project` re-implements the archive-aware project-column read added as `_row_projects` at :1856 in the same file, leaving two queries that must be kept in step while `_row_projects().get(run_id)` already answers the one-row case.

non-blocking: `negative_control_note` says the base arm names "every id the done-when names", but logs/base-ledger.log fails test_complete_command_assumes_utc_for_a_naive_completion_stamp and not test_explicit_promotion_stamp_reaches_every_duration_consumer, so the red population measured at f4403247ef is not the eight ids the done_when states at a80ca2b63f.
